newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI announces new regulatory measures.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI announces new regulatory measures.

text.p: India's market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), on Monday announced steps aimed at efficiently regulating and increasing liquidity in the stock markets.
SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told reporters after a board meeting in the Indian capital that it would ask short sellers to report their short sales position at the end of each day.
"The short seller must be asked to declare his position on short sales at the end of the day," Mehta said.
"Stock exchanges should impose appropriate margins on short sales."
Mehta said the decision to implement the rules had been taken in principle, but the exact details would be worked out by a panel of experts within three weeks' time.
"Occasionally there are cases of bear hammering. Action of this kind would prevent such incidents occuring. We are performing our role as a regulator," Mehta told Reuters after the news conference.
Mehta said the federal government would soon approve a stock lending scheme which would allow banks and financial institutions to lend funds to brokers.
This would increase liquidity in the market, taken together with the SEBI's measures on short sales.

SEBI also amended a regulation requiring custodians to have a minimum net worth of 500 million rupees. The custodians would be allowed to increase their net worth to 500 million rupees in a phased manner over a period of five years, it said.
The market regulator announced measures to revive the Over the Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI).
It has decided to permit all companies to trade on the OTCEI. Mehta said the 250-million-rupee cap on firms registering on OTCEI had been lifted.
The SEBI said it had decided to accept some of the recommendations of the Dave panel of experts on OTCEI trading.
The equity shares of all unlisted companies would be allowed to be traded on the OTCEI, it said.

SEBI also accepted a recommendation by the panel that companies with no record of having paid dividends in three successive years of the previous five and which have not been appraised by financial institutions be allowed to raise funds by listing on OTCEI.
But these companies have to fulfill two conditions -- they must be sponsored by an OTCEI member and must appoint at least two market makers to provide continuous liquidity to the stock.
"OTCEI was an exchange with beautiful features but was not performing. We appointed a committee which gave these recommendations, which hopefully would be reviving OTCEI," Mehta said.
